gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Xebec Tri-Screen 3 ($699) needs Xebec's own Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter ($59 today, normally $99) on every Mac, because macOS does not support MST. The adapter uses DisplayLink and its driver, so a MacBook owner pays $758, nearly double the $433.49 the Mobile Pixels store charges today for the Trio 3 Pro.
standout_why: I compared three pages: rottenwifi.com (11 best triple portable monitors, cited, prices 'current as of Nov 9 2026'), sekin.in (cited) and uperfect.com's blog (cited). Rottenwifi and Sekin each say only that a Xebec Mac adapter is 'sold separately' or 'may be sold separately'. Neither gives its price, says it is required for all Macs, or says it uses DisplayLink. UPERFECT's blog lists the Xebec at $699.99 and does not mention the adapter. All three rival pages, and ChatGPT's answer at $469.23, show the Trio 3 Pro above the $433.49 the maker charges today: Rottenwifi and Sekin both show $509.99, and Sekin observed that price on Aug 18. None of the pages gives an all-in price for a Mac owner.
decides: This confirms Trio 3 Pro as the pick and widens its lead. At $433.49 (list $599.99) it costs $324.50 less than a Mac-ready Xebec Tri-Screen 3, which has smaller 13.3-inch 1080p screens. It costs $43.50 more than the UPERFECT BE14BF ($389.99), and UPERFECT's own blog says the BE14BF needs a driver download for single-cable use. The FOPO S788 we list costs $699.99, so the pick doesn't go to it on price. It only makes sense for a shopper who wants three 16-inch screens.
